採用・広告の製品.quote: Vision AI engineered for your product - Neurala

Neurala’s patented L-DNN™ technology runs the entire AI workflow at the edge, trains on a handful of images, and integrates directly into your hardware or software stack. No cloud. No massive datasets. No compromise on privacy.
Patented technology. Proven in production.

Our Lifelong Deep Neural Network (L-DNN)™ is designed from the ground up to run inside real products, in real environments — without the constraints that make conventional deep learning impractical for deployment.

L-DNN reaches high accuracy with dramatically less training data than conventional neural networks. Where standard models require thousands of labeled examples, Neurala’s technology learns from a small number of representative images and continues learning as new data becomes available.

The full loop — training, adaptation, and inference — runs on-device, on standard processors such as Intel i3 or higher, with no GPU required. End users can train custom models using their own data, on their own hardware, without sending anything to the cloud.

Privacy in Neurala is architectural, not a configuration option. Image data is processed and stored locally by design. It never touches an external server. For OEM partners in regulated or security-sensitive industries, this is a hard requirement. Neurala meets it without compromise.
Every environment is different. We work directly with your engineering team to understand your hardware, your use case, and your customers — then package our technology to fit precisely.

We learn your stack in depth: hardware constraints, target environment, end-user requirements, and where vision AI needs to live within your product architecture. No assumptions. No generic solutions.

We package Neurala’s L-DNN into a software library built specifically for your environment. This isn’t configuration — it’s engineering. The output is a tailored integration that fits your product exactly.
You ship a product with embedded vision AI that works reliably, at the edge, from day one. Our team remains available through deployment and beyond. A partnership doesn’t end at handoff.

Neurala developed a customized model-training application for Sony's AITRIOS marketplace that allowed users to train and deploy purpose-built vision AI models for use with Sony's AI-enabled IMX500 vision sensor. This tool made it simple and easy for any user to build custom vision AI models that could run on the edge on smart cameras with Sony's IMX500 sensor.

apetito deployed Neurala’s L-DNN technology across their production facility to detect missing meal components before trays leave the line. 30 custom vision AI models were built and deployed, with new models trainable in as little as 10 minutes without AI expertise. The model developed to detect missing Yorkshire pudding achieved 100% accuracy in testing.

Neurala was founded in 2006 by neuroscientists whose research for NASA, DARPA, and the Air Force Research Labs led them to a simple but radical question: what if AI could learn the way biological brains do? That question became a patented technology now deployed inside enterprise products around the world.
enterprise partners globally

In 2013, Neurala emerged from stealth and joined the Techstars program to begin commercial deployment. Today, Neurala’s L-DNN technology is embedded inside products built by FLIR, Sony Semiconductor Solutions, IHI, and more — and we are actively working with integrators and OEM hardware companies to put L-DNN inside the next generation of intelligent products.
Neuroscientist and entrepreneur. Max led Neurala from founding through its commercial growth phase, combining deep research expertise with a hands-on approach to building the company.
Computational neuroscientist and architect of L-DNN. Anatoli leads Neurala and holds primary responsibility for the patented technology at the core of every partnership.
To make powerful vision AI accessible — deployable on inexpensive hardware, trainable from minimal data, and embeddable in the products that people actually use.

As Head of Research, Matt leads the development of next-generation AI technologies with a focus on edge intelligence, automated visual inspection, and adaptive learning systems.
